claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization.
Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has a coercive field no greater than approximately 100 Oe.
Aging fcc FeCoNi at approximately 500–600 °C for about 1–5 hours can induce incipient spinodal decomposition.
The proposed aging treatment can form coherent nanoscale precipitates or chemical fluctuations within the fcc matrix.
The proposed nanoscale precipitates or chemical fluctuations will be approximately 5–10 nm in size.
The nanoscale chemical heterogeneities act as domain-wall pinning centers.
Domain-wall pinning by the aging-induced nanoscale heterogeneities increases coercivity.
The proposed aging treatment will increase the coercive field above approximately 100 Oe relative to untreated single-phase fcc FeCoNi.
The proposed aging treatment will leave saturation magnetization largely unchanged relative to untreated single-phase fcc FeCoNi.
The overall fcc matrix can be retained while producing the proposed nanoscale heterogeneities.
Avoiding a complete phase transformation is necessary for the proposed intervention.
Room-temperature hysteresis measurements by VSM or SQUID can be used to compare coercive field and saturation magnetization between aged and untreated samples.
